resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1864 date belongs to the white pyramidal beacon that the form and LighthouseFriends both date to 1864. The lit light dates from 1872 (LighthouseFriends); the form dates the present brick tower to 1873. These two dates are not reconciled here.

notes_for_editor: Unresolved: (1) First lit: LighthouseFriends gives 20 November 1872; the 1981 form dates the present tower to 1873; the station record gives 1864 (the beacon). The story gives both 1872 and 1873 and does not choose. (2) Lens: the form says the lens was converted in 1960 from a fourth-order Fresnel; the 1916 and 1917 Bulletin entries (as LighthouseFriends prints them), the USLHS record and LighthouseFriends all give a fifth-order lens. Not settled. (3) Characteristic and range: the station record says Fl R 10s and 3 nm; LighthouseFriends says a red flash every fifteen seconds visible eleven nautical miles. Not checked against the Light List, which was not read. (4) Access: the 1981 form (road ends at Herring Cove Beach, National Park Service limits) and LighthouseFriends (walk the breakwater and sand) describe different routes; the LighthouseFriends page is undated. (5) USCG Historian article on Wood End Lighthouse: the live page refused access (HTTP 403); archived copies at the 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2024 capture years were not found. (6) Newspapers: Chronicling America search (1872 to 1935, MA) returned two Worcester pages (1872, 1877) whose reads timed out; nothing from them is used. (7) The 1889 Boston Globe interview with Lowe, the 1935 ice-bound report, the 1930 water supply and the Lowe biography are LighthouseFriends' account of newspapers that were not read directly; footnoted to LighthouseFriends. (8) The Life-Saving Service station at Wood End (1896) is a separate station with its own rescue record; its rescue tables were not used. (9) The station record's 'listed 1987-06-15' was not confirmed from a read source (the form's receipt stamp is OCR-damaged), so no NRHP listing event is recorded. (10) The 1915 pennant list is for fiscal 1914 and the flags list for fiscal 1915; the story uses 'pennant' and 'flag' as each source does. (11) Roster names: Thomas Lowe, Philip R. Smith and the other roster names are the USLHS archive's own spellings; no alternative spelling was found. (12) Column-matched names checked on page images: the 1921 flags table (PDF p. 14, printed p. 174) reads 'Wood End, Mass' with 'Philip R. Smith' in the 2d-district row. The 1917 flags list (PDF p. 2) reads 'Philip R. Smith' on the Wood End line; its OCR is letter-spaced, so no OCR quote is used for it. (13) The 1981 form records the exterior as painted white; LighthouseFriends says brown. Both are stated. (14) The 1921 flag list is for calendar 1920 (Bulletin of 1921); the 1917 list is for the fiscal year 1916 (Bulletin text). (15) The 1981 form's access note (four-wheel-drive only; National Park Service restriction) sits beside LighthouseFriends' walking route; the story recommends no visit route. (16) The 1981 form's own 1875 entry reads 'more than fifty ships'; LighthouseFriends' 'over fifty shipwrecks since 1875' is kept as its own claim.
